source_text: Dehinc manus imponitur, per benedictionem advocans et invitans Spiritum sanctum. Sane humano ingenio licebit spiritum in aquam arcessere et concorporationem eorum, accommodatis desuper manibus, alio spiritu tantae claritatis animare; Deo autem in suo organo non licebit per manus sanctas sublimitatem modulari spiritalem? Sed est hoc quoque de veteri sacramento, quo nepotes suos ex Joseph Ephraim et Manassem Jacob, capitibus impositis et intermutatis manibus, benedixerit, et quidem ita transversim obliquatis in se, ut Christum deformantes, jam tunc portenderent benedictionem in Christum futuram. Tunc ille sanctissimus Spiritus super emundata et benedicta corpora libens a Patre descendit, super Baptismi aquas, tanquam pristinam sedem recognoscens, conquiescit, columbae figura delapsus in Dominum, ut natura Spiritus sancti declararetur per animal simplicitatis et innocentiae, quod etiam corporaliter ipso felle careat columba. Ideoque: Estote, inquit, simplices sicut columbae, ne hoc quidem sine argumento praecedentis figurae. Quemadmodum enim post aquas diluvii, quibus iniquitas antiqua purgata est, post Baptismum (ut ita dixerim) mundi pacem coelestis irae praeco columba terris adnuntiavit dimissa ex arca, et cum olea reversa; quod signum etiam apud nationes paci praetenditur: eadem dispositione spiritalis effectus terrae, id est carni nostrae emergenti de lavacro post vetera delicta, columba sancti Spiritus advolat, pacem Dei afferens, emissa de coelis, ubi Ecclesia est arca figurata. Sed mundus rursus delinquit, quo male comparetur Baptismus diluvio. Itaque igni destinatur, sicut et homo qui post Baptismum delicta restaurat, ut hoc quoque in signum admonitionis nostrae debeat accipi.
pass_a_gloss: Then the hand is laid on, through blessing calling and inviting the Holy Spirit. Indeed, it will be permitted to human ingenuity to summon the spirit into the water and to animate their incorporation, with hands accommodated from above, with another spirit of such great clarity; but will it not be permitted to God in His own instrument to modulate spiritual sublimity through holy hands? But this also is from the old sacrament, by which Jacob blessed his grandchildren, Ephraim and Manasseh, sons of Joseph, with hands imposed on their heads and interchanged, and indeed in such a way, with them turned obliquely towards himself, that they, deforming Christ, already then portended the future blessing in Christ. Then that most holy Spirit willingly descends from the Father upon the purified and blessed bodies, over the waters of Baptism, as if recognizing His former seat, and rests, having fallen in the form of a dove upon the Lord, so that the nature of the Holy Spirit might be declared through an animal of simplicity and innocence, which dove also lacks bile even corporally. And therefore: Be, He says, simple as doves, not even this without argument from the preceding figure. For just as after the waters of the flood, by which ancient iniquity was purified, after Baptism, so to speak, the dove, a herald of heavenly wrath, announced peace to the earth, having been sent out from the ark, and having returned with an olive branch; which sign is also held out to the nations as a sign of peace: by the same disposition, the spiritual effect on the earth, that is, on our flesh emerging from the bath after former sins, the dove of the Holy Spirit flies, bringing the peace of God, sent from heaven, where the Church is the figurated ark. But the world again sins, by which Baptism is compared unfavorably to the flood. And so it is destined for fire, just as also the man who after Baptism restores sins, so that this also ought to be taken as a sign of our admonition.

pass_b_english: Then the hand is laid on, calling and inviting the Holy Spirit through a blessing. Human ingenuity may claim the right to summon a spirit into the water and animate the union of the baptized by placing hands on them, using some other spirit of great clarity. So will God not be allowed to modulate spiritual sublimity through holy hands in His own instrument? This also comes from the old sacrament, by which Jacob blessed his grandchildren Ephraim and Manasseh, the sons of Joseph, by laying hands on their heads and crossing them over—turning them obliquely toward himself so that, in distorting the figure of Christ, they already foreshadowed the future blessing in Christ (Genesis 48:14). Then that most holy Spirit descends willingly from the Father upon the purified and blessed bodies, over the waters of Baptism, as if recognizing His former seat, and rests there, having come down in the form of a dove upon the Lord, so that the nature of the Holy Spirit might be declared through an animal of simplicity and innocence—a dove that even physically lacks bile. And therefore: 'Be simple as doves,' He says; not even this command is without support from the preceding figure. For just as after the waters of the flood, by which ancient iniquity was purged, after Baptism, so to speak, the dove—a herald of heavenly wrath—announced peace to the earth when sent out from the ark and returned with an olive branch, a sign still held out among nations as a pledge of peace: by the same arrangement, the dove of the Holy Spirit flies to the spiritual effect on the earth, that is, on our flesh emerging from the washing after former sins, bringing the peace of God, sent from heaven where the Church is figured as the ark. But the world sins again, which makes Baptism compare poorly with the flood. And so it is destined for fire, just as the man who restores his sins after Baptism is; this too must be taken as a sign of our warning.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the source. The scripture citation (Genesis 48:14) added in Pass B is a correct identification of the event described in the Latin text (Jacob blessing Ephraim and Manasseh).
